blocks.title: Governance
blocks.text:
Processing Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit registered in the State of New York. Governance describes how the Foundation is structured, who makes which decisions, and how the organization holds itself accountable to the communities it serves.

The Foundation's work is funded by grants, sponsorships, and donations. As an open-source software nonprofit, the organization depends on both paid and volunteer labor to carry out its projects. Funders, contributors, and the public are entitled to know how decisions about those resources and projects are made and who is accountable.

blocks.title: Organizational Structure
blocks.body: Processing Foundation is composed of a **Board of Directors**, a **Team** of staff, **advisors and mentors**, and **steering and advisory committees**, each with a distinct scope.

blocks.title: Board of Directors
blocks.body:
The Board of Directors sets the organization's mission, strategic plan, and fundraising strategy, informed by their experience in the creative industry, open-source software, and education. The Board approves the annual budget, monitors legal compliance, and appoints the leadership.

The Board has eight members, who serve three-year terms. Terms are staggered to preserve institutional knowledge. The existing Board elects new directors, and members of the Team may put forward nominations.

Meeting quarterly, the Board's meeting minutes and resolutions are maintained by the Foundation.

blocks.title: Team
blocks.body: The day-to-day operations of the Foundation are carried out by two Co-Executive Directors, an Engineering Team, a Programs Team, and an Operations Team. The Team executes the strategic and fundraising plans set by the Board.

statements.title: Co-Executive Directors
statements.description:
Set organizational direction, lead fundraising, and are accountable to the Board for the Foundation's operations and finances.

- Roxana Hadad, Co-Executive Director
- Xin Xin, Co-Executive Director

statements.title: Engineering Team
statements.description:
Maintains and develops p5.js and Processing Java, the software at the center of the Foundation's mission, while supporting the contributor communities that build alongside them.

- Kit Kuksenok, p5.js Project Lead and Engineering Manager
- Moon Davé, Processing Project Lead

statements.title: Programs Team
statements.description:
Designs and runs the fellowships, community events, and educational programs through which people encounter and learn these tools.

- Amy B. Woodman, Senior Program Manager
- Raphaël de Courville, Processing Community Lead
- Qianqian Ye, Director of Creative Technology

statements.title: Operations Team
statements.description:
Manages the Foundation's finances, communications, and administration so that program and engineering work can run reliably.

- Charles Reinhardt, Finance Manager
- Camille Wong, Communications Manager

blocks.title: Advisors & Mentors
blocks.body: Advisors and mentors are individuals with outside expertise brought in to support specific areas of strategy, fundraising, or operations. Unlike the Board of Directors, advisors and mentors have no formal voting power or decision-making authority.

blocks.title: Steering Committees
blocks.body: Steering Committees hold decision-making authority over the projects and resources within their scope, including budget, resource allocation, and technical direction.

blocks.subtitle: p5.js Shared Responsibility Committee
blocks.body:
The Shared Responsibility Committee (SRC) governs p5.js. It is a joint decision-making body with members from both Processing Foundation and the p5.js contributor community, working toward the shared goal of making p5.js more accessible.

Processing Foundation and p5.js share many resources: volunteer time, funding, staff, operational costs, community goodwill, and software artifacts. While the values of Processing Foundation and p5.js align, their resources and costs may differ. The p5.js SRC was created to manage those shared resources and costs, and to make decisions through open consensus with a public record.

The SRC holds decision-making authority over p5.js, including budget and resource allocation, as well as technical and software direction. Processing Foundation members of the SRC ensure that decisions are financially responsible and legally compliant; community members ensure that decisions reflect the needs of the people who build and use p5.js.

The SRC decides by open consensus and maintains a public record of its decisions on GitHub.

SRC members are appointed and elected by existing committee members.

**Members:** Amy B. Woodman, Dave Pagurek, Kenneth Lim, Kit Kuksenok, Xin Xin

intro.title: Advisory Committees
intro.description:
Advisory Committees provide feedback on program strategy and fundraising plans. They do not hold decision-making authority.

Both committees convene according to their program cycle. Members are appointed and elected by the existing members of each committee. Committee members who are not members of the Foundation Team serve one-year terms and may serve consecutive terms.

intro.title: Non-Governing Bodies
intro.description: Equally important as governing members are the people and organizations without governing power who contribute essential work to support Processing Foundation and its projects.

statements.title: Creators
statements.description: Processing Foundation's core tools were started and advanced by creators whose vision shaped what the software became.

statements.title: Contributors
statements.description: Contributors support the open-source tools in critical ways by writing code, documentation, translations, and tutorials. They support community forums by reporting bugs, answering questions, and moderating project discussions. Contribution alone does not grant a role in governance. The Processing Foundation team and the SRC go through an internal process to recognize and nominate maintainers and committee members.

statements.title: Sponsors
statements.description: As a nonprofit, Processing Foundation depends on financial contributions from foundations, corporations, and individual supporters. To protect the independence of the projects and the organization, sponsors hold no role in governance. Sponsorship does not influence technical direction, program decisions, or organizational strategy.

statements.title: Vendors
statements.description: Processing Foundation contracts with vendors for specific services such as accounting, nonprofit tax filing, legal counsel, and hosting. Vendors do not have governing power, and the Operations Team manages these relationships.

statements.title: Contractors
statements.description: Processing Foundation engages contractors for a defined scope of work, including engineering, design, and programs. Contractors carry out work directed by the Team or the relevant committee and hold no governance role by virtue of their contract.
